phase_or_sample: Hexagonal CeCo3B2-type, P6/mmm, Ru kagome net, a = 5.475 Å, c = 3.027 Å; arc-melted polycrystalline bulk; powder XRD fits the structure apart from a minute elemental-Ru peak
page_table_or_figure: Read in arXiv:2512.16945v2, published as Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308 (2026). Pages are arXiv PDF pages. p.1: abstract. p.2: Methods (stoichiometric 1:3:2 mix), Fig. 1 (XRD), shielding fraction close to 100%, magnetization onset 0.70 K at 5 Oe. p.3: Fig. 2 (susceptibility) and the specific-heat jump text. p.4: Table I (Tc = 0.81 K), Fig. 4 (Cp) and Fig. 5 (resistivity). p.5: resistivity reaches zero near 0.84 K.
measurement_method: DC magnetization (MPMS with He-3, demagnetization corrected, Nd = 1/3), specific heat (PPMS with dilution refrigerator, down to 60 mK, fields up to 800 Oe), resistivity (50 mK to 300 K)
synthesis_conditions: Y, Ru and B (each 99.99%) weighed in the stoichiometric 1:3:2 ratio, arc-melted on a water-cooled Cu hearth under Ar and remelted several times; mass loss negligible
evidence_note: Stoichiometric arc-melted YRu3B2 is a bulk superconductor at ambient pressure, with about 100% shielding and a zero-field specific-heat jump at 0.81 K. Mater. 9, 025013 (10.1088/2515-7639/ae6a72), Tc 0.63 K from Cp and 0.7 K from resistivity. Tc criterion: Zero-field specific-heat jump, the value listed as Tc in Table I. Magnetization onset at 5 Oe is 0.70 K; resistivity reaches zero near 0.84 K.

phase_or_sample: Misfit layer compound (PbSe)1.14NbSe2, with a rock-salt PbSe bilayer alternating with one NbSe2 layer. Bulk as-grown CVT single crystals. XRD (00l) shows only the misfit layer spacing of 12.31 ± 0.01 Å (Fig. 1d). Raman A1g/E2g modes shift from 2H-NbSe2 values (226.4/236.4 to 222.4/256.2 cm-1, Fig. 1e). XPS on the cleaved surface shows Pb, Nb and Se peaks (Fig. 1c). Normal-state resistance is about 2.5 mΩ (Fig. 2a), as expected for a bulk crystal rather than an exfoliated flake. Ambient pressure.
page_table_or_figure: Re-read myself in arXiv:2304.12230v1. arXiv lists only v1, with journal ref 'Phys. Rev. Mater. 7, L041801 (2023)' matching the Crossref title and authors. p.1: abstract (Tc = 5.6 ± 0.1 K). p.2: CVT growth, Fig. 1 (XPS, XRD, Raman), and the quoted Tc sentence. p.3: Fig. 2(a), R(T) with Tc = 5.6 K at 90% R_N. On the plotted curve the onset is about 5.8 K and zero resistance about 4.7 K, read from the rendered figure. Fig. 2(b-d) shows data in field. p.5: the summary repeats Tc = 5.6 ± 0.1 K. The Supplemental Material (Figs. S1-S5, Table S1) is not in the arXiv PDF and was not read.
measurement_method: Electrical resistance versus temperature, in zero field and with in-plane fields up to 9 T and out-of-plane fields up to 3.5 T. ARPES, XPS, XRD and Raman for characterisation. The main text has no magnetization or specific-heat data.
synthesis_conditions: Single crystals grown by chemical vapour transport, with precursors, transport agent and temperature gradient optimised (Supplemental Table S1, not read). Stoichiometry is fixed by the ratio of the mismatched a-axis periodicities.
evidence_note: (PbSe)1.14NbSe2 = Pb1.14NbSe3.14, within 0.04 at.% of the row on every element. Bulk as-grown CVT crystal at ambient pressure; R(T) reaches zero near 4.7 K. Tc criterion: 90% of normal-state resistance (Fig. 2(a) caption). Caveats: resistive only (no magnetization or specific heat in the main text), and 5.6 K is above the 1.1 to 2.5 K of earlier bulk reports the authors cite; the superconductor label is better supported than the Tc value.

phase_or_sample: Bulk single crystal of tetragonal P4/nmm (PbO-type) Fe1+ySexTe1-x with x = 0.45, nominal y = 0.03, grown by a modified Bridgman method. It is labelled Fe1.03Se0.45Te0.55 in Fig. 2(b) and Fig. 4(b), and the Fig. 4 caption reads Fe1.03SexTe1-x. Neutron powder diffraction on ground crystals finds 97% main P4/nmm phase. Static incommensurate magnetism coexists below about 5.5-7 K in about 75% of the muon volume. The authors find no macroscopic phase separation: the SC and magnetic volume fractions add up to more than 1.
page_table_or_figure: I re-read arXiv:0907.3429v2 myself. Its abstract page gives the journal reference Phys. Rev. B 80, 140511(R) (2009) and the DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.80.140511, and Crossref's title and 14 authors match. Pages below are arXiv PDF pages. p.1: methods, phase purity (97% for x = 0.45), and the statement that x = 0.45 is a bulk superconductor with chi_AC = -1.18 at about 2 K. p.2: Fig. 1, chi_AC(T) for x = 0.45 (open blue circles). p.3: 'superconductivity occurs throughout the bulk of the x = 0.45 and 0.5 crystals'. p.4: Fig. 4(b), SC volume fraction of Fe1.03Se0.45Te0.55, and Fig. 4(g), Tc onset and Tc mid versus x for Fe1.03SexTe1-x.
measurement_method: AC susceptibility (Quantum Design PPMS, 0.1 mT, 1000 Hz, ab plane parallel to the field) down to about 2.3 K; ZF/TF/LF muon-spin rotation down to 1.7 K; neutron powder and single-crystal diffraction
synthesis_conditions: Modified Bridgman growth. Fe, Se and Te powders (at least 99.99%) were mixed in the appropriate ratios, pressed into a rod and vacuum-sealed in a double-walled quartz ampoule. The rod was melted and homogenised at 1200 C for 4 h, cooled in an 8 C/cm gradient at 4 C/h down to 750 C, then at 50 C/h. The composition is nominal.
evidence_note: Fe1.03Se0.45Te0.55 is within 0.04 at.% of the row. Bulk superconductor in the paper's words: chi_AC = -1.18 at about 2 K and a superconducting volume fraction near 1 (Fig. 4(b)). Tc criterion: onset of the ac-susceptibility transition, 13.0 K, read by the verifier from Fig. 4(g) (midpoint 9.1 K); the text prints no number for x = 0.45. Caveats: nominal composition, 3% impurity phase, coexisting magnetism, broad transition.

phase_or_sample: Bulk polycrystalline as-cast arc-melted alloy. One of seven comparison alloys at e/a about 4.7, which the paper reports all 'randomly arrange on BCC lattices' and show 'a single homogeneous superconducting phase'. No XRD pattern is shown for this particular alloy.
page_table_or_figure: Fig. 6 (legend entry, lavender ZFC curve and caption) and the text below it, arXiv:1610.03746v1 p. 12. The BCC statement is on p. 11, the composition definitions are on p. 5, and the experimental section is on p. 4. The version of record is PNAS 113(46) E7144 (2016), Fig. 6, which I could not open.
measurement_method: DC magnetization, zero-field-cooled, mu0H = 2 mT, Quantum Design PPMS DynaCool with the VSM option. Plotted as normalised M(T)/M(0). No resistivity or specific heat for this composition.
synthesis_conditions: Stoichiometric pure metals (Nb 99.8%, Zr 99.6%, Hf 99.6%, Ti 99.95%) arc-melted at high current (T > 2500 C) under argon with a co-heated Zr-sponge getter. Melted five times and turned over each time; weight loss insignificant. Rapidly cooled on a water-chilled Cu plate. As-cast, no anneal reported. Ambient pressure.
evidence_note: [Nb]0.67(ZrHfTi)0.33 in the paper = Nb0.67Hf0.11Zr0.11Ti0.11, an exact match. Its own measured zero-field-cooled curve in Fig. 6 shows one sharp transition at Tc about 9.2 K (onset about 9.4 K); the text says these comparison alloys are single-phase bcc. Caveats: read in the arXiv preprint (PNAS and PMC blocked); no XRD or shielding fraction shown for this alloy.

phase_or_sample: Sn-flux single crystal, EPMA CaFe1.94Co0.06As2; ThCr2Si2 type, I4/mmm, a = 3.8875(1) A, c = 11.687(1) A; phase-pure by powder XRD of crushed crystals
page_table_or_figure: arXiv:0810.0848v2 (accepted version of PRB 79, 012504): p.1 abstract, growth, EPMA and XRD; p.2 Fig. 1(a) inset (diamagnetic onset at 17 K in 0.005 T; 55-60% volume fraction) and Fig. 2(a) lower inset and 2(b) (resistive Tc 17 K, zero resistance up to 8 T); p.3 Figs. 3-4 (Hc2; no discernible Cp jump)
measurement_method: Anisotropic dc susceptibility (0.005 T and 0.5 T), resistivity (J parallel to [100], 1.8-300 K, fields up to 14 T), heat capacity (1.8-300 K), 57Fe Mossbauer
synthesis_conditions: Sn-flux solution growth, Ca:Fe:Co:As:Sn = 1:1.8:0.2:2:19 in alumina inside evacuated quartz; 1050 C for 24 h, slow cool to 450 C over 3 weeks, then rapid cool; flux centrifuged
evidence_note: The formula is the table row (Co 0.013, Fe 0.387). The paper's crystal is CaFe1.94Co0.06As2 by microprobe (Co 0.012, Fe 0.388), 0.1 at.% from the row, inside the rule's 0.15 at.%; that composition is already a superconductor in the table (15.4 K). Tc 17 K from the onsets of diamagnetism and of the resistive drop; zero resistance; 55 to 60% shielding. Caveat: Ca(Fe,Co)2As2 at this Co level depends on processing; some Sn-flux crystals nearby keep the SDW and lack bulk superconductivity (Hu et al., arXiv:1111.7034), while an annealed crystal at x = 0.033 shows a specific-heat jump (Ran et al., arXiv:1204.5457).
